deviations: RD columns (2)-(3) use the optimal bandwidths reported in the paper (25/30/13 for number of cosponsors, 16/24/11 for percent opposite) rather than the bandwidths from rdrobust::rdbwselect (mserd, bill level), which the script also computes and prints (e.g. 17.8 for Republicans/number of cosponsors, 25.0 for Democrats/percent opposite).
Macro-area dummies were built from ICPSR state codes (Northeast 1-14, Midwest 21-37, South 40-56, West 61-82), since no region variable is in the data. Log population density = lnpop - lnarea.

Rookie = tenure_run == 1; committee leader = chair (comc) or ranking member (comr); occupation dummies occ1-occ5 (unknown and miscellaneous form the base); total bills sponsored = count of bills per sponsor-Congress in the analysis file.
Percent of cosponsors from the opposite party = 100 * pct_cosponsors_opposite, set to 0 for bills with no cosponsors.

Propensity scores come from logits estimated at the bill level within each party subsample. The full-sample IPW columns use district characteristics + |MV1_democrat| (+ sponsor characteristics in column 5). The RD+IPW score uses district characteristics only, within the bandwidth. Weights are 1/p for female sponsors and 1/(1-p) for male sponsors.
fixest drops one fixed-effect singleton (minor topic), so N is 1 lower than the paper's for some cells (60669 vs 60670).
notes: Data: AnalysisData/bills_analysis_101-111_replication.dta only. Column 1 is OLS (feols) of the outcome on the female-sponsor dummy, sponsor characteristics, district characteristics, 33 committee-of-referral dummies, and Congress and minor-topic fixed effects, with SEs clustered by sponsor-Congress. Column 2 is a local-linear RD on MV1_female with separate slopes on each side and Congress FE, in mixed-gender races within the bandwidth. Column 3 adds bill characteristics and IPW weights to the column 2 regression. Columns 4-5 are weighted regressions on the full sample with Congress FE and bill characteristics. One exploratory run (attempt-1) inspected the variables. The first estimation run is the final one: check_attempt reported all claims within tolerance, and the script was not changed afterwards.
